advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the environment holds BOTH a tracker genesis key and a deployment override key, and a cert signed under the NON-first key (e.g. genesis-signed while override is set) still certifies — exercising the multi-element trust root.
evidence: Commit message: 'take every key the environment holds as the trust root (`allowed_signers_from_keys` already accepts a list), so a box in transition between a genesis key and a deployment key can certify either.'

src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:279-280: `pubs = [_read_opcert_pub(kp) for kp in _opcert_own_key_paths(tracker)]` / `return list(dict.fromkeys([p for p in pubs if p]))` — returns a list intended to hold multiple keys.
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:559: `trust_root = authorship.allowed_signers_from_keys(own_pubs, principal)` now receives the full list.

ABSENCE: test_bound_signer... (line 100) has only a bound deployment key; test_key_path_override... (line 114) has only an override key with tracker genesis absent; test_certifies_when_the_key_dir_is_read_only (line 127) has only an override key; test_tracker_genesis... (line 144) has only the tracker key. No test creates an environment holding BOTH a genesis tracker key AND an override/binding key at once, so the multi-element own_pubs / multi-signer trust root is never asserted.
advisory.finding: The multi-key trust-root path — the heart of the fix, where _opcert_own_public_keys returns >1 key so 'a box in transition between a genesis key and a deployment key can certify either' — is never exercised. Every test has exactly one signing key present, so own_pubs always has length 1 and allowed_signers_from_keys is never driven with multiple keys. A regression that dropped all but the first resolved key (e.g. off-by-one in the dict.fromkeys dedup, or reverting to a single-key resolution) would still pass all four tests.
scenarios: A box mid-migration holds both a `<tracker>/.opcert-key` (genesis) and a `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` deployment key; a cert signed under the genesis key must still certify while the deployment override is set (and vice versa).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that signs a cert under the tracker genesis key, then sets REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH to a second (deployment) key present on the box, and asserts verify_signature still returns verdict == 'certified' — and the symmetric case (deployment-signed cert while a tracker genesis key also exists).
